threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think getting on the 243 is a good idea during rush hour. Bless your heart, but it’s a sardine can for a reason.
Caught the N133 last night; two blokes at the back arguing over who saw a ghost in Brockwell Park. The driver just shook his head, no eye contact.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I spotted a guy dressed as a pigeon doing yoga in the park, I realized this place has its own rhythm and beats.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you catch a U-Bahn on a Monday morning while the city’s in chaos from a transit strike. The empty trains feel like a ghost town.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You'll notice true locals jump out of the way of a runaway skateboard without missing a beat, while newcomers just stand there, bewildered.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: The 14-Muni bus sat at 16th and Mission for 20 minutes because the driver was arguing with a passenger about the fare. Classic.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all hipster cafes but miss the little bakeries that open at dawn, still serving the same croissants since the 80s.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the group of newcomers standing in front of the Metro map, squinting at the lines like it’s a treasure map with no ‘X’ in sight.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the tube' – locals know it's just 'the Overground' once you hit Clapton.
Caught the N68 last night and saw a guy arguing with the driver about a missing stop—turns out he was on the wrong bus all along.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a guy juggling flaming torches on Richardplatz while a toddler inspected a stray cat. Only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you see a techno party break into a spontaneous street performance, with dancers and drum circles spilling onto the asphalt.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they can tell you the difference between a taco from La Taqueria and one from El Farolito, even in the dark.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus with a guy singing karaoke on his phone. He hit every note while the driver just rolled her eyes. Classic San Francisco moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think the Gràcia street parties are just for fun, but they often highlight local issues we face year-round that they overlook.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're new by the way they order 'café amb llet' and look confused when it arrives as a tiny cup instead of a mug.
